status: Local behavior, library, client, affected integrations and ten API campaigns passed; immutable installed acceptance pending
problem: Strategic combat search received only the automatic damage assignment. With 5 damage against a defending Poro (3 Might) and Playful Phantom (5 Might), it killed Poro and left Phantom, even though assigning all 5 to Phantom was legal.
change: A bounded beam explores lethal-first orders using public unit information. Strategic evaluates these as ordinary actions and uses the highest estimated removal-value legal allocation during combat rollouts. The default UI allocation and rules validator are unchanged.

bounds.depth: number of opposing units at the combat battlefield
bounds.caveat: Bounded search, not exhaustive for arbitrary boards. Root evaluation resolves real effects; rollout allocation uses a public board-value estimate.

coverage: Both seats: choose larger threat and forecast the same trade
Both seats: trade against multiple units and incorporate damage already marked
96 four-defender positions compare candidate membership to independently enumerated orders validated by real actions
Both seats: Tank + Backline can be first or last, never between ordinary units
Both seats: 17-defender boards, bounded legal candidates, hidden-information independence and no mutation by planning
78 Block decision cases spanning two seats, all three difficulties, and 1 through 13 attacking Might
focused.oracle: Two-defender Block expectations specify surviving physical units, battlefield control and whether Block remains in hand; enemy allocations independently maximize removed printed Might. The four-defender oracle checks enumeration agreement, not independent proof of the rules validator.

rules_review.scope: Lethal-first assignment, existing damage, final-unit excess, Tank/Backline priority and postcombat healing. No new damage replacement mechanics are admitted.

corrections: Expanded test v4 did not compile because the temporary keyword enum was imported from the wrong module; v5 corrects the test import.

All ten API runners produced passing reports. The first comparison harness assumed difficulty was stored on every record; the format runner stores it on paired groups and uses explicit easy/tactical/strategic ordering for future matches. Reconciled completed reports without rerunning games.
limitations: No claim of expert strength or complete Standard parity.
Search can prune strategically useful orders on crowded boards; its public value heuristic does not independently price every card ability.
Rollouts still assume no further discretionary responses and settle with bounded choice policies.
Existing Relaxed and Tactical behavior is retained; measured Block misses are documented.
Full card coverage and beginner learning outcomes remain unfinished.
external_code: No external implementation or test code copied.

complete_game_coverage.registered_game_count: Not captured by this passing run; successful test stdout is suppressed.

regressions.scope: All library/client tests plus c4_play, irelia_arito, irelia_decisions, registered_matches, strategic_api, turn_keywords_matches. Other integration binaries remain for the immutable release gate.

api.limits: Trace changes demonstrate different decisions, not improved win rates or stronger general play. Both Strategic Block/Yuumi series still observe no Yuumi trigger.
